articles.headline: Rest-of-season rankings: Cousins, Jefferson, Mendoza biggest deadline winners
articles.description: Need to make or assess a trade offer? With the NFL trade deadline passed, these rankings are designed to help.
articles.headlineJa: シーズン残り期間のランキング：トレード期限の最大の勝者はカズンズ、ジェファーソン、メンドーサ
articles.descriptionJa: トレードの提案を行いたい、あるいは評価したいですか？NFLのトレード期限が終了した今、これらのランキングがその助けとなります。
articles.body:
Each week, Eric Karabell ranks players by position based on their fantasy football value for the rest of the 2026 season. Use the information to optimize the players for their future potential and/or to gauge their value in trade. Eric's top 100 can be found below the positions in this column. 

Quarterback

Rankings changes: There is movement in the top 12, as Jordan Love forces his way into the top five, C.J. Stroud returns to the top 10 new Vikings starter Kirk Cousins gets a nice bump into QB1 range. Cousins has enjoyed a strong season, fifth at QB in fantasy points, and the Vikings enjoy a friendly schedule the rest of the season. Unlike with the Raiders, Cousins avoids losing his starting role to No. 1 draft pick Fernando Mendoza, who also moves way up, as he inherits the starting role.

Meanwhile, Jared Goff tumbles a bit after consecutive misfires with single-digit points. Matthew Stafford lost another star receiver, which must affect his value, while Jacoby Brissett resumes starter status in a new place, Baltimore. For those in deeper leagues and superflex formats, rookies Carson Beck and Kyle McCord are starters for the Cardinals and Dolphins, respectively, as is unproven Joe Milton with the Eagles. Keep an eye on what the Colts, Chargers and perhaps Seahawks do the next few weeks as well.

Running back

Rankings changes: Bucky Irving continues his rise, pushing further into the top 10, while Derrick Henry continues his fall, moving more outside of it. Jonah Coleman is in the top 20, while Ashton Jeanty is barely holding onto his spot. There is much uncertainty at running back, with managers left to guess what will happen with the Packers with Josh Jacobs (finger) out, and there is little clarity with the Patriots, Saints, Giants, Commanders and Eagles situations.

Wide receiver

Rankings changes: Injuries are the story here, with Puka Nacua (knee), one of the top picks in preseason drafts, out for at least the rest of the fantasy regular season and perhaps more, while promising Michael Wilson (neck) is done for the season. Learn the names Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and Reggie Virgil.

Multiple Colts were traded and, naturally, individual value rises to WR4 levels -- at least -- as they head to playoff teams. Keenan Allen should see more volume with Brock Purdy and the 49ers, while Josh Downs should pile on receiving yards with Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs. Justin Jefferson adds value with his QB change. Finally, rookies KC Concepcion, Jordyn Tyson and Caleb Douglas move up. Tank Dell and Mack Hollins rejoin the rankings.

Tight end

Rankings changes: There is no movement in the top 10. Later, Darren Waller and AJ Barner enjoyed excellent Week 9 outings, though they remain inconsistent and difficult to trust. It's time to move on from Jake Ferguson (ankle).

articles.body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline passed Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET, and we covered every deal up until that point.

Before this week, big names to be dealt included DT Jeffery Simmons to the Bears, QB J.J. McCarthy to the Giants, QB Jacoby Brissett to the Ravens and CB Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys.

On Monday, the Jaguars traded for safety Jessie Bates III, defensive tackle Davon Godchaux and defensive tackle Jordan Davis. The Lions also added safety help with Andre Cisco.

On Tuesday, the 49ers and Chiefs shored up their WR rooms by trading for former Colts Keenan Allen and Josh Downs, respectively. The Vikings got some much-needed QB help by trading a 2027 third-round pick for Raiders' Kirk Cousins. And the Broncos boosted their linebacker room with Chargers' Daiyan Henley.

At the buzzer, the Ravens and Falcons also swapped interior offensive linemen. Center Ryan Neuzil is headed to Baltimore, while guard Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick are headed to Atlanta.

We tracked all in-season moves and trade-related buzz right through the deadline. The most recent deals and intel will be added at the top.

Cardinals trade QB Brissett to Ravens

Ravens get: QB Jacoby Brissett, 2027 fifth-round pick

The Cardinals finalized a trade to send QB Jacoby Brissett to the Ravens on Friday. The Cardinals are sending a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-rounder in exchange for Brissett and a 2027 fourth-round selection.

Brissett's first start as the Ravens' starting quarterback could come as soon as Week 10 when Baltimore hosts the Chargers on "Monday Night Football." He was recently benched by the Cardinals before the trade.

The Bears are acquiring All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Titans, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter. The Titans are receiving 2027 and 2028 first-round picks, plus a 2027 fourth-round pick from the Bears in exchange for Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick, the sources told Schefter.

Simmons, 29, signed a three-year, $105.8 million extension with $100 million guaranteed with the Titans in June. He is under contract through the 2030 season.

articles.body:
NFL analysts Ben Solak and Seth Walder are grading deals from the 2026 trade deadline, which passed at 4 p.m. ET Tuesday.

When grading trades, we evaluate them for each team based on on-field impact, cap implications, draft compensation and effects within the context of a team's overall short- and long-term outlooks. How confident are we in knowing if this is a good or bad decision? And how big is the impact of this decision? Both questions play a role in our grades, though a low-impact decision can still receive a strong or poor grade. Even with lower stakes, clear-cut wins or losses still matter.

Here are our evaluations for 16 deals so far, including three Jaguars trades from Monday, three quarterback moves for teams in need and multiple deals involving at least one first-round pick.

Jump to a trade:

Henley | Hooker | Cousins | Allen

Davis | Godchaux | Cisco | Bates

Brissett | Simmons | Buckner | Nelson

Harrison | Jurgens | Porter | McCarthy

Chargers trade LB Henley to Broncos

Broncos get: LB Daiyan Henley

Chargers get: 2027 fourth-round pick, 2028 fifth-round pick

Broncos: C+

Chargers: B+

The winless Chargers finally (!) decided to trade a player before the deadline, dealing Henley, a player in the final year of his contract, to the division-rival Broncos.

It's an interesting deal because linebacker did not look like a particular need for Denver. Alex Singleton leads all linebackers in run stop win rate this season and Justin Strnad is a good coverage player. Henley's numbers are OK this season. He ranks in the 46th percentile and has allowed 0.9 yards per coverage snap (average for the position) per NFL Next Gen Stats.

I think it's reasonable for Denver to be adding at the deadline, but this is not trivial draft capital to give up for a player who is going to provide depth or be part of a rotation.

I'm on board with this move for the Chargers. While Henley could have been a player they kept around given that he will only turn 27 later this month, he wasn't a difference-maker that they had to hang on to. And if he left in free agency, they would not have recouped this value via a compensatory pick even if they had gotten one -- which was also unlikely given their considerable 2027 cap space.

On the other hand, Denver does have a decent change to recoup a compensatory pick if Henley walks, with both Singleton and Strnad signed into 2027 or later (though Singleton will turn 33 next month).

Some will criticize the Chargers trading a player within the division, but that is foolish. If anything, the teams the Chargers should most want to take draft capital from ought to be other teams in the AFC West.

The only real question for the Chargers -- why didn't they trade away more players?

Bills get: S Amani Hooker, 2027 fifth-round pick

Titans get: 2027 second-round pick

Bills grade: C+

Titans grade: A-

articles.headline: Fantasy buzz: Malik Willis placed on IR, are there any Dolphins you should start?
articles.description: What does the Miami Dolphins' fantasy football outlook show with starting QB Malik Willis placed on IR?
articles.headlineJa: ファンタジー・ニュース：マリク・ウィリスがIR入り、起用すべきドルフィンズの選手はいるか？
articles.descriptionJa: 先発QBのマリク・ウィリスがIR入りしたことで、マイアミ・ドルフィンズのファンタジー・フットボールの見通しはどうなるのか？
articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Nov. 10: Malik Willis placed on IR

By Michael F. Florio

The Miami Dolphins placed Willis on the IR Tuesday due to a groin injury, and he will miss a minimum of four games.

Willis has averaged 13.1 fantasy PPG while throwing 1,396 yards, six touchdowns and six interceptions. He has run for 232 yards and three touchdowns. While he disappointed in fantasy last week against the Detroit Lions, he was trending upwards having thrown five of his six touchdown passes in the past four games.

With Willis out, that leaves Kyle McCord as the Dolphins starter. Not only will that be his first career start, McCord has not thrown a pass in the NFL. Willis was a potential streaming option due to the matchup, but that does not apply to McCord.

Additionally, fantasy managers should avoid the Dolphins pass catchers. Malik Washington had been a safe-floor flex option with Willis while Caleb Douglas has flashed his upside at times. Both could be benched -- or even dropped if you have a roster crunch -- until we see that they can produce with McCord. Ollie Gordon II is the only Dolphin that should be started in fantasy football for the time being. Gordon has averaged 13.2 fantasy PPG since Week 3 and the Dolphins have the second-best remaining fantasy RB schedule.

The Buffalo Bills D/ST, which added Amani Hooker on Tuesday, will be a top streaming option in Week 10. Buffalo's defense has scored 16 and 15 fantasy points in their last two games, both of which also came against backup QBs. They are just 34% rostered and should be a priority target this week for those who play the streaming defense game.

Nov. 10: Cook helps Bills overcome tough Vikings defense

By Michael F. Florio

Despite a valiant effort by the Minnesota Vikings' defense, the Buffalo Bills' offense won out on Monday night. James Cook III was the lone standout performance, rushing 31 times for 107 yards and a touchdown. Only Jahmyr Gibbs has run for more yards against the Vikings this season. Cook finished with 16.7 fantasy points, enough to be the RB8 for the week. His 31 carries are the second most in any game in Cook's career.

Josh Allen had his worst fantasy night of the season, finishing with only 12.86 fantasy points. He threw for just 234 yards, with one touchdown and one interception. He also ran the ball six times for 15 yards. That was actually the most fantasy points any QB has scored against the Vikings since Jordan Love in Week 1 (19.48). Allen has a bounceback opportunity next week against the New York Jets.

articles.headline: 2026 NFL trade deadline winners, losers: From Kirk Cousins to the Bengals
articles.description: Which teams made the best -- and worst -- moves before the NFL trade deadline? We're making sense of all the action.
articles.headlineJa: 2026年NFLトレード期限の勝者と敗者：カーク・カズンズからベンガルズまで
articles.descriptionJa: NFLトレード期限前に、どのチームが最善の、そして最悪の動きを見せたのか？一連の動きを読み解きます。
articles.body:
The NFL trade deadline has come and gone. I will forever remember it as the trade deadline in which the Bengals nearly accidentally spent a third-round pick on Arnold Ebiketie (more on that below). 

Identifying winners and losers on deadline day is always tough. The Titans, Howie Roseman and Josh Downs will be made winners and losers for their efforts today not by my words, but by the picks they make or games they win over the next two or three years. Of course, we can grade the quality of their work now (spoiler, they are winners) -- but this isn't the real test. The real test is what comes next.

I have six winners and four losers from this year's trade deadline ranging from players to GMs. Let's dive in.

Jump to:

Cousins | Jefferson | Bengals 

Downs | Roseman | Taylor | Poles

 Titans | Chargers | Cardinals

Deadline winner: QB Kirk Cousins

Cousins is about to have a quarterbacking season for the ages.

No, he won't set the passing touchdown record or anything. But let's trace the arc here.

Cousins started nine games for a 4-5 Raiders team that was waiting to turn the page to 2026 No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza. The entire time he started, he comported himself with the exact attitude and perspective you'd hope to see from a veteran bridge starter.

"If I'm not the best option, then I don't want to be out there," Cousins said in late October after the Raiders' fourth-straight loss. "The organization will do what they feel is best, but I feel that Fernando's done a great job and has a bright future ahead. I'm gonna try to go out there and play as well as I possibly can to help us win and give him a great example to learn from until he does go out there eventually."

A beautiful quote. And it echoes what Cousins has said from the beginning: he was in Las Vegas to help the team win, but to also give Mendoza an example of how to prepare, speak, compete and perform as an NFL quarterback. If Mendoza looks competent at any part of the 2026 season (and even beyond), Cousins will receive the share of credit due an angel investor. Even if Mendoza was always destined to play well -- he's the first overall pick, for crying out loud -- Cousins and the Raiders' patient approach with Mendoza will be lauded as a contributing factor.

So, Cousins has that going for him. His arc continues to Minnesota where the power of friendship welcomes him with open arms. Cousins was a Viking from 2018 to 2023, the last two seasons of which were spent under rookie head coach Kevin O'Connell. The Vikings went 13-4 in 2022 under Cousins before he tore his Achilles midway through the 2023 season.

O'Connell's offense isn't just good for Cousins, it's almost built in the image of Cousins. O'Connell was the quarterbacks coach with Washington in 2017, Cousins' final season on the team. articles.headline: MrBeast, meet Haaland: Man City star puts YouTuber through soccer gauntlet
articles.description: Manchester City star Erling Haaland has collaborated with popular YouTuber "MrBeast" in a series of various soccer challenges.
articles.headlineJa: MrBeastがハーランドと対面：マン・シティのスターがYouTuberにサッカーの試練を与える
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティのスター、アーリング・ハーランドが、人気YouTuberの「MrBeast」とコラボレーションし、一連の様々なサッカーチャレンジを行った。
articles.body:
Manchester City star Erling Haaland is known for his extraordinary feats on a soccer pitch, but this time he decided to put that to the test by allowing famous YouTube star James Stephen "Jimmy" Donaldson -- better known as "MrBeast"  -- to participate in a series of intense soccer challenges known as the "Erling Haaland Gauntlet" at the club's training ground.

Posted on the Norway international's YouTube channel, which currently has over four million subscribers, Haaland put MrBeast -- alongside his two friends Tareq Salameh and Nolan Hansen -- through several soccer challenges to test their skill, strength and endurance. 

The challenges consisted of sprints, wall sits, headers and a crossbar challenge, in which the winner would get a "Haaland Hammer," and the loser would have to go into goal and get hit by free shots from the penalty spot.

In the end, it was Salameh who ended up winning the "Haaland Hammer" after finishing first amongst the three, and it was MrBeast who had the misfortune of getting hit with shots from his two friends and, of course, Haaland.

It's safe to say that the most-subscribed YouTuber with over 526 million -- who's known for his extraordinary challenges -- probably doesn't have what it takes to cut it as a professional soccer player. 

While it is currently the international break, that doesn't mean Haaland will relax while there are no matches for Manchester City. The 26-year-old was called up to play for his national team this month against Wales and Denmark in the final matches of their UEFA Nations League A campaign.

They are currently last in Group 4, as they look to qualify for the quarterfinal of the competition.

NBA Trade Lab updates: Former teammates join Luka in LA?

The Los Angeles Lakers find themselves at the top of the Western Conference standings, with Luka Doncic playing like the best player in the world and leading the way in ESPN's Net Points Metric (NBA Net Points Awards -- ESPN Analytics). Their BPI projected win total (2026-27 Projections NBA Power Index -- ESPN) that started the season at 45 has already increased to 53. They completely retooled their roster this past offseason after losing Lebron James in free agency to the Philadelphia 76ers, but their newly added pieces have gelled together quickly to leave fans around the league re-thinking what the ceiling of this team could be.

After sending out two first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps in the Walker Kessler sign-and-trade (Lakers trade for Jazz C Walker Kessler, sign trio, sources say -- ESPN), the Lakers are very limited in remaining draft capital they could use to add another major piece through a trade. Lakers get: P.J. Washington

articles.headline: Sources: Warriors lose Brandon Williams to mild hamstring strain
articles.description: Warriors will be without reserve guard Brandon Williams for at least a week after he strained his left hamstring during Monday night's win, sources told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者発表：ウォリアーズ、ブランドン・ウィリアムズが軽度のハムストリング肉離れにより離脱
articles.descriptionJa: 関係者がESPNに語ったところによると、ウォリアーズは、月曜夜の勝利の際に左ハムストリングを痛めた控えガードのブランドン・ウィリアムズが、少なくとも1週間欠場することになる。
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors will be without reserve guard Brandon Williams for at least a week after he strained his left hamstring during Monday night's 138-87 win over the New Orleans Pelicans, team sources told ESPN.

Williams entered late in the first quarter, burst to the rim for two quick layups but came up hobbled on the second and limped to the locker room after only 99 seconds of action.

The Warriors soon announced that Williams was out with a hamstring issue and scheduled for an MRI. Those results revealed the mild strain, ruling him out for the Warriors' difficult upcoming road trip to Houston, San Antonio, New Orleans, Dallas and Memphis.

 

Williams has been an immediate bench spark in his first season with the Warriors, averaging 10.4 points and 2.3 assists in only 16.4 minutes per game, providing scoring punch the moment Stephen Curry rests. Williams has 17 and 20 points in the two games that Curry missed this season, including a win over the LA Clippers as part of the Warriors' current eight-game win streak.

But left hamstring issues have followed Williams early in his NBA career. He strained it in the 2025 preseason while with Dallas and subsequently missed time last March while dealing with tightness.

The Warriors, while surging at 8-3, are significantly depleted. Starting wings Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody are rehabbing serious knee injuries, projected starting center Kristaps Porzingis has stepped away from basketball entirely and they lost backup guard Will Richard to a UCL tear in his left thumb over the weekend.

articles.descriptionJa: エリック・カラベルが、NBA界隈で注目している事項と、それがファンタジー・スポーツにどのような影響を与えるかをまとめる。
articles.body:
It's easy to claim otherwise today, but there was little indication Cleveland Cavaliers PG/SG James Harden would suddenly become a fantasy disappointment this season. After all, Harden was terrific last season, averaging 43.5 ESPN fantasy points per game. Only 16 players scored more. Harden was 36 years old.

Is there really much difference between being 36 and 37 years old? (Guess I will find out in a few years when I turn 37, lol.) Harden may not have deserved a second-round slot in ESPN average live drafts, but there was regression built into projections and he fell to Round 4.

Harden is 11 games into the season and he's not performing as a top-50 fantasy option, certainly not yet anyway at 29.1 fantasy points per game, and many are whispering that this is the end of his time as a top point guard. It is fine if Immanuel Quickley, Fred VanVleet or Coby White average 15.3 PPG, 4.8 RPG and only 5.7 APG, but certainly not if Harden does so.

Perhaps we didn't expect quite another 20.5 PPG, 4.8 RPG and 7.7 APG (his numbers in 26 games with the Cavaliers after the LA Clippers trade), but the current numbers are just not cool.

Is it reasonable to ask if this is all we're going to get this season? Perhaps it is, but there is a bigger picture going on with Cleveland. Harden has only 13 assists and nine turnovers in his past three outings, only one of them a win (over the Philadelphia 76ers, of course).

He won't shoot a ghastly 36.4% from the field for long, but watching Harden and his missing usage it is clear he is more willing to defer shots and in directing the offense. His field goal attempts are down from 16 per game to 12, and free throw attempts down from 7.5 per game to 4.8. His minutes are also down. Hmm.

Typically, this would be a wise time to trade for Harden, so I will gently side with that one, with some caveat: It would be quite surprising if Harden finishes among the top 20 fantasy scorers again. Then again, the Cavaliers may be pacing all their stars for better playoff performance.

Who is earning Cleveland's shots? SG/PG Donovan Mitchell has seen his usage crumble as well, scoring 22.8 PPG, when last season it was 27.9 PPG. Even PF/C Evan Mobley is underachieving across the board, as he falls even further from potential 20-PPG, 10-RPG production.

Perhaps the Cavaliers are handling things perfectly here. The bench is certainly improved, with impressive second-round rookie SG Meleek Thomas hitting 47.8% of his 3-pointers and Croatian journeyman SF Mario Hezonja, back in the NBA after six seasons overseas, contributing a useful 19.9 MPG. Newcomer SF/PF Peyton Watson, who was more valuable in fantasy as a Denver Nugget last season, has solidified a starting role.

Yes, Harden (and to a lesser extent Mitchell and Mobley) are disappointing fantasy managers, but that appears to be, in a roundabout way, Cleveland's actual plan.

articles.headlineJa: シャビ・シモンズ、復帰が近づく中、スパーズでのACL負傷による精神的苦痛を明かす
articles.descriptionJa: 怪我に泣いたトッテナムのアタッカー、シャビ・シモンズは、昨シーズンのチームの降格争いを目の当たりにした苦悩について語ったが、ロベルト・デ・ゼルビ率いるチームへの復帰に向けて「果てしない時間」をトレーニングに費やしている。
articles.body:
Injured Tottenham attacker Xavi Simons has spoken of the anguish he felt watching the club's relegation battle last season, but is working "endless hours" to return for Roberto De Zerbi's side.

Xavi sustained anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) damage during a 1-0 win at Wolves on April 25 which ruled the Netherlands playmaker out of Spurs' final four fixtures along with the World Cup last summer.

However, Xavi, 23, has been ahead of schedule through his rehabilitation and is set to enter phase three of his recovery later in November, which will allow him to resume team training.

Last month, the former Barcelona and Paris St Germain youngster was invited to speak at the Oxford Union and went into detail about his current spell on the sidelines.

Speaking on Oct. 30, Xavi told students: "I had to watch the remainder of the season from my hospital bed and let me tell you it was not easy.

"I felt completely out of control, infuriated because I couldn't contribute and help. I couldn't do a thing. Luckily the boys did their job.

"Mental is just as important as physical. I've had bad moments at night, not even my family know how bad. I've cried, I've wanted so bad to contribute to Spurs, to my national team.

"I read books, I enhanced my knowledge on certain things, I wanted more information, I wanted to stimulate my mind. I wanted calmness in my brain. That was as important as going to the gym every day.

- Tottenham's winning run brought to abrupt end by late Noah Okafor winner

- Leeds condemn 'disgusting' alleged racist abuse of Jayden Bogle after Spurs game

"It's ultimately finding the balance. You can't underestimate the importance of good psychological health. If your brain isn't working, your body isn't working."

ACL ruptures generally have a recovery time of around nine months, but Xavi is in line to feature in first-team training again after the international break.

That would put him back in contact training only seven months after suffering the injury and raises the possibility of a return to competitive action before the nine-month mark at the end of January.

Quizzed during a question-and-answer session about how he plans to return at his best, Xavi said: "My knee has to feel good. I need to feel strong. Right now, I'm on track, I'm getting stronger every day.

"I'm putting in endless hours. I have a great team that has been with me this entire journey. Everyone has a different schedule.

"Everyone's journey is different. For me, I want to come home and only think, 'I can't move my legs anymore,' because I have pushed myself to the limit daily.

"I want to feel tired. That feeling is when I allow myself to rest. That's how I've approached it throughout."

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Arsenal to offload three players, with Atlético Madrid keen
articles.description: Atlético Madrid are one of the main clubs showing an interest in Arsenal midfielder Martín Zubimendi, while Viktor Gyökeres and Mikel Merino could also depart. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
The Arsenal trio of Martín Zubimendi, Viktor Gyökeres and Mikel Merino could depart to raise funds for more arrivals, while Barcelona have made an enquiry about signing Bayern Munich center back Jonathan Tah. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Atlético Madrid are one of the main clubs showing an interest in Arsenal midfielder Martín Zubimendi, as confirmed by Diario Sport. There is a good relationship between the two clubs and Los Colchoneros' interest in the 27-year-old stretches back to his time with Real Sociedad, while the Gunners need to offload players to help balance their books. Viktor Gyökeres and Mikel Merino could also leave the Emirates to help Arsenal's finances, according to AS. The trio have all struggled for playing time this season.

- Barcelona have made an enquiry about signing Bayern Munich center back Jonathan Tah, as reported by Sky Sports Deutschland. The Blaugrana are focusing on the 30-year-old ahead of January, with the club's sporting director Deco looking for an experienced defender who can play alongside yoiung Pau Cubarsí and bring stability and leadership qualities. Bayern have little interest in letting Tah leave, especially as he is a key part of their plans and has a contract that runs until 2029, while the Germany international is also not considering a transfer.

- Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur are interested in Real Sociedad striker Orri Óskarsson, according to Calciomercato. The 22-year-old has caught the eye with his performances this season, already having 14 goals and six assists to his name across LaLiga and the Europa League. The Red Devils are interested due to Benjamin Sesko's injury absence, while Spurs are looking for a striker to suit Roberto De Zerbi's style of play. Everton, Brentford and Sunderland are also interested in Óskarsson, while Atalanta have previously been linked, though any offer to sign the Iceland international would need to exceed €20 million.

- Liverpool and Real Madrid are on a growing list of clubs monitoring Brighton & Hove Albion goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen, according to TEAMtalk. The Reds are looking at the 24-year-old as they plan for whenever veteran stopper Alisson Becker departs Anfield, while Los Blancos see the Netherlands international as a possible successor to Thibaut Courtois. Chelsea and Manchester United are also long-term admirers, while Bayern are also tracking his progress having previously made enquiries.

- Juventus are looking at Atlético's Alexander Sørloth, Monaco's Folarin Balogun and Al Qadsiah's Mateo Retegui as they aim to sign a striker in the January transfer window, according to Gazzetta dello Sport. Sørloth in particular is a favorite for Juve, who have held a long-term interest in the 30-year-old.
